subject: Wanted Poster Board
findings: The State Historical Society of Missouri catalogs Thomas Theodore Crittenden’s 1881 proclamation offering rewards for the arrest of Frank and Jesse James (C2875). The linked broadside was actually viewed.

The actual broadside is typographic: a large condensed heading, contrasting display type, horizontal rules and smaller paragraphs. It contains no portrait, no decorative gun border and no dead-or-alive slogan. Preserve this distinction from modern souvenir posters.

The photograph shows age-darkened paper; that is not evidence that newly printed 1881 stock had this yellow colour. A future period reconstruction should distinguish paper/ink from later damage and aging.

The proclamation supports a reward-notice object, but does not establish the design of a freestanding Western notice board. Board construction and period posting context remain unsourced; no completed render brief or asset is claimed.

Any future reveal effect must wait for authoritative public reveal. A private Wanted Poster Board peek must not change a face-down model, public poster, portrait or History identity. The generic holding scene must not imply that every revealed historical crew member was wanted as a criminal.

sources.role: State Historical Society contextual essay and link to the actual proclamation; use arrest/reward wording from the object rather than assuming the section heading describes its text.
Actually viewed colour photograph of the surviving broadside; typography only, no board depicted.

next_evidence_needed: A documented nineteenth-century American posting surface/board with visible construction; then compose a conservative reconstruction with explicit limits. No art generation or reveal code change was made.

followup_2026_10_08.construction_evidence: 1871 New York Clipper account, transcribed by the Circus Historical Society: lumber boards erected by carpenters, bills pasted onto them.
followup_2026_10_08.interpretation: A compact two-post stand is explicitly reconstructed, not a discovered photograph or exact replica. Prior findings above record the earlier research state.
